coverage_notes: Fresh run, no prior checkpoint existed for 2026-08-31. Primary-source-first sweep on Payten / Asseco SEE. NEW ROUTE DISCOVERED: asee.io exposes two custom WordPress post types beyond /posts — /wp-json/wp/v2/press_release (English financial press releases) and /wp-json/wp/v2/fin_press_release (Polish) — which is how the Q2/H1 2026 release of 27/07/2026 was found; the Tier-0 competitor_news.json cache only enumerates the standard /posts type and therefore MISSED it entirely. Recommend adding both post types to the Tier-0 collector. Opened and text-extracted with pdfminer: the H1 2026 Management Report (published 31/07/2026, uploaded to /wp-content/uploads/2026/08/) and the Q2 2026 investor presentation — these gave segment revenue in EUR, per-country revenue, per-line POS/ATM/IPD/ECR revenue, backlog as at July 2026, the M&A notes and the full subsidiary schedule. Confirmed on asee.io's investor calendar that the next trigger is the Q3 2026 consolidated report on 26/10/2026. asee.io /posts feed re-enumerated: NOTHING published since 30/06/2026, so no new asee.io news in the 24/07-31/08 delta window. payten.com re-checked: it is NOT WordPress (custom nginx site, no sitemap, JS-rendered article bodies) but WebFetch renders it fine this run (the TLS chain error logged in the previous two runs did not recur) — its five newest items were read and dated; latest is 16/06/2026, and the Halkbank Skopje SoftPOS date previously flagged as unanchored is now confirmed at 17/03/2026 from the dated primary article. NEW SOURCE FOUND: monri.hr and monri.com are live WordPress feeds for Payten's Monri Payments brand, with items through 18/08/2026 — neither is in the Tier-0 cache; recommend adding. NEW SOURCE FOUND AND USED: crz.gov.sk (Slovak Central Register of Contracts) is fully fetchable with a desktop UA and returns supplier-name search results with date, contract name, value, supplier and buyer — this surfaced the previously untracked SONET Slovakia POS-framework stream and settled the Asseco Central Europe question (its 2026 Slovak buyers are tax, health-insurance, energy and security agencies, i.e. NOT Printec-competitive). Serbian angle worked through the NBS 2026 procurement plan PDF (version 9 of 9 located by probing the /propisi-tend/2026/ path) plus a company-registry confirmation of PIB 110428879. Local-language searching run in Serbian, Croatian, Slovenian and Montenegrin; no Payten/NLB or Payten/Hipotekarna 2026 development surfaced in local press, and Hipotekarna's 'MojPOS' softPOS app could not be attributed to Payten (four candidate Google Play package ids all 404). GENUINE GAPS: (a) no per-country ATM or POS unit counts exist in any Payten/ASEE disclosure and none were estimated, per the playbook; (b) the subject and value of the Payten-NBS contract are genuinely unpublished because Serbian below-threshold/exempt contracts are not published — this is a disclosure gap, not a search failure; (c) no Payten announcement of any kind fell inside the 24/07-31/08 delta window, so the delta is carried entirely by the H1 earnings disclosure, the Slovak contract register and the Monri feed.
access_issues: nbs.rs: the procurement section is not at /sr/o_nbs/javne-nabavke/ or any of four path variants tried (all HTTP 404); resolved by probing the known document path https://www.nbs.rs/export/sites/NBS_site/documents/propisi/propisi-tend/2026/Plan_nabavki_2026_vN.pdf, where v1-v9 return 200 and v10 returns 404 — v9 downloaded and text-extracted. Two of those probes timed out at 25s mid-download (slow origin), so use a >=120s timeout. After roughly a dozen requests nbs.rs served a Serbian-language block page ('Pristup blokiran! ... ID vaseg slucaja: 2294493387326416126') to https://www.nbs.rs/sitemap.xml — rate limiting, so throttle nbs.rs to a few requests per session. jnportal.ujn.gov.rs (Serbian public procurement portal): the site root returns 200 but /api/notice-search returns HTTP 401, so the portal cannot be queried without credentials — this blocked confirmation of the Payten-NBS contract subject and value. www.payten.com: /wp-json/wp/v2/posts redirects in a loop to a 404 (the site is not WordPress); /sitemap.xml returns an HTML shell, not XML; article bodies are client-side rendered so curl returns only the shared header, footer and contact block — resolved by using WebFetch, which rendered every article and returned dates. NOTE for the record: the TLS 'unable to verify the first certificate' failure logged against payten.com in the 2026-07-15 and 2026-07-24 runs did NOT recur this run via WebFetch, though curl still needs -k. www.uvo.gov.sk/crz/api/v1/zmluvy returns an HTML page rather than JSON, so the UVO API was abandoned in favour of crz.gov.sk HTML search, which worked. crz.gov.sk individual contract pages (/zmluva/<id>/) load but their detail tables resisted extraction; the search-results listing carries the same fields and was used instead. Google Play: four candidate package ids for Hipotekarna Banka's MojPOS softPOS (com.payten.hipotekarna, com.payten.softpos.hipotekarna, me.hipotekarnabanka.mojpos, com.hipotekarnabanka.mojpos) all returned 404, so the app's builder is unattributed. No source was silently dropped.

Beograd-Novi Beograd) against buyer Narodna banka Srbije for 2026 and return the contract subject, value and signature date — this is the one materially unresolved fact on this competitor. 2) The two Slovak SONET framework contracts with a real commercial ceiling — Kancelaria Narodnej rady SR contract 26/2026 (EUR 49,999.99, https://www.crz.gov.sk/zmluva/12228902/) and Mesto Zvolen 854/2026 (https://www.crz.gov.sk/zmluva/12649737/) — have downloadable contract PDFs on those pages; an operator should pull them to establish SONET's per-transaction pricing model and which terminal hardware brand it deploys, which is directly actionable for Printec's Slovak POS pricing. 3) If a Bloomberg/Refinitiv or WSE-filing terminal is available, retrieve the full ASEE S.A. H1 2026 consolidated interim financial statements (not just the management report) for the segment note in PLN alongside EUR, to cross-check the EUR segment figures used here.

signals.entity: Asseco SEE / Payten (ASEE Group) — regional DIRECT competitor
signals.country: Regional (RS, HR, BA, ME, SI, RO)
signals.signal: ASEE Group's H1 2026 Management Report (published 31/07/2026) shows the Payment Solutions segment — the Payten line that overlaps Printec — fell to EUR 102.8m in H1 2026, down EUR 5.2m (-5%) YoY, and to EUR 51.4m in Q2 (-7%). The decline is attributed line-by-line AND country-by-country: the ATM line (sale and maintenance of cash machines) lost EUR 3.4m in H1 'primarily from lower equipment deliveries in South-Eastern Europe, particularly in Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Montenegro', with Central Europe also negative 'mainly due to reduced deliveries in Romania'; the POS line (delivery and maintenance of payment terminals) lost EUR 1.9m, mainly Western Europe and, within SEE, 'lower deliveries in Slovenia and Croatia'. Offsetting growth came from the IPD (independent POS network) + ECR (electronic fiscal cash register) lines, +EUR 2.7m, of which +EUR 2.4m in SEE. Segment figures are disclosed in EUR; the statutory financial statements are in PLN.
signals.source_name: ASEE Group — Management Report on Operations for the 6 months ended 30 June 2026 (PDF; publication date stated in the report as 31/07/2026)
signals.implies: Printec's most direct regional rival has publicly conceded that its ATM hardware and POS terminal deliveries shrank in six of Printec's own footprint countries in the same half-year. That is the clearest opening in two years to attack Payten-held ATM estates and POS acceptance accounts in Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia, Montenegro, Slovenia and Romania with NCR dispense/intelligent-deposit/recycling hardware, x-core multivendor ATM software and Verifone/Castles terminals plus TMS — and to argue to those banks that their incumbent is quietly de-prioritising hardware refresh in favour of software, fiscal cash registers and merchant services.
signals.likelihood: Already disclosed and contemporaneous; gives an immediate 6-12 month displacement window before Payten's next refresh cycle
signals.followup: Ask each named-country Printec country manager which Payten-supplied ATM contracts fall due in 2026-27; re-check the Q3 2026 report (due 26/10/2026) to see whether the ATM line recovers or the retreat is structural.

signals.entity: Asseco SEE S.A. (ASEE Group / Payten) — group earnings
signals.signal: ASEE Group's estimated Q2/H1 2026 results (press release, Warsaw, 27/07/2026): Q2 sales EUR 101.4m (+1%), H1 sales EUR 203.0m (+3%). Q2 by segment: Payment Solutions EUR 51.4m (-EUR 3.8m YoY), Banking Solutions EUR 22.6m (+EUR 4.0m, ~+22%), Dedicated Solutions EUR 27.4m (+EUR 0.4m). Q2 operating profit EUR 15.3m (+27%), EBITDA EUR 22.8m (+25%). H1 operating profit EUR 29.0m (+21%), EBITDA EUR 42.6m. CEO Piotr Jelenski attributes the profit jump to Banking Solutions and states the Payment Solutions weakness 'reflected lower results in business lines related to ATM and payment terminal sales and services', partly offset by 'independent payment terminal networks and fiscal cash registers'. All segment figures are quoted in EUR.
signals.source_name: ASEE press release — 'ASEE Group Delivers 27% Increase in Operating Profit in Q2 2026' (asee.io newsroom, press_release post type)
signals.implies: Payten is now a profitable software-and-services company whose hardware/terminal business is shrinking — so it will bid Printec's ATM and POS tenders on price to defend installed base, but will not chase volume hardware. Printec should compete on total-cost-of-ownership and managed/field services (where it is strong) rather than assume Payten is an aggressive hardware bidder, and should expect Payten to counter-attack in core banking, digital onboarding and fraud, where its margins are rising fast.
signals.likelihood: Confirmed; next earnings trigger is the Q3 2026 consolidated report on 26/10/2026
signals.followup: Diary the ASEE Q3 2026 report for 26/10/2026 (confirmed on asee.io's investor calendar) and re-key Payment Solutions vs Banking Solutions plus any country attribution.

signals.country: Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia & Herzegovina, North Macedonia, other SEE, CEE
signals.signal: The Q2 2026 investor presentation discloses ASEE Group H1 2026 revenue by country/region in EUR millions (H1 2026 vs H1 2025): Serbia 53.8 vs 47.7 (+13%), Croatia 33.9 vs 31.1 (+9%), Bosnia & Herzegovina 16.4 vs 17.3 (-5%), North Macedonia 11.3 vs 8.8 (+29%), other SEE entities (stated in the deck as Albania, Bulgaria, Kosovo, Montenegro, Slovenia) 14.4 vs 14.7 (-2%); SEE total 129.8 vs 119.6 (+9%); Central Europe (Czech Republic, Poland, Slovakia, Romania, Moldova, Ukraine) 29.3 vs 27.0 (+8%); Western Europe 21.9 vs 25.7 (-15%); Turkey 21.0; group EUR 203.0m. The same deck splits Payment Solutions H1 revenue by line: POS 37.1, ATM incl. IAD (independent/off-premise ATM deployment, i.e. the MoneyGet network) 22.6, eCommerce+Processing 29.6, ECR+IPD 13.5.
signals.source_name: ASEE Group — 'Financial results of ASEE Group for Q2 2026' investor presentation (PDF)
signals.implies: This is a rare hard scale reading on Printec's closest regional rival country by country. Serbia (EUR 53.8m) and Croatia (EUR 33.9m) are where Payten is strongest and best defended; Bosnia (-5%) and the Albania/Bulgaria/Kosovo/Montenegro/Slovenia cluster (-2%) are where it is going backwards and where Printec's ATM, recycler and managed-services pitch has the least entrenched opposition. The ATM+IAD line at EUR 22.6m for a whole half-year across all markets shows Payten's ATM business is modest in absolute terms — Printec should not concede footprint ATM tenders to it by reputation alone.
signals.likelihood: Standing disclosure until the Q3 update on 26/10/2026
signals.followup: Build a Printec-vs-Payten revenue-share view per footprint country from this table; prioritise BiH and the Montenegro/Albania/Kosovo cluster for 2026-27 ATM and recycler campaigns.

signals.signal: The Q2 2026 investor deck publishes backlog (order book) as at July 2026, excluding hyperinflation effects and the India/Dubai operations. Payten alone: FY2026 forecast revenue backlog EUR 189.0m vs EUR 185.4m a year earlier (+2%), with margin backlog EUR 164.0m vs EUR 151.3m (+8%); but Q3 2026 forecast revenue backlog is EUR 44.6m vs EUR 46.9m (-5%). ASEE + Payten combined: FY2026 revenue backlog EUR 379.2m vs EUR 367.1m (+3%), margin backlog EUR 298.7m vs EUR 278.5m (+7%); Q3 2026 combined revenue backlog EUR 92.7m vs EUR 102.1m (-9%). ASEE Banking + Dedicated Solutions Q3 2026 backlog EUR 48.1m vs EUR 55.2m (-13%).
signals.source_name: ASEE Group — Q2 2026 investor presentation, backlog slides (PDF)
signals.implies: Payten's contracted revenue for the coming quarter is falling while its margin backlog rises — a company protecting price over volume. For Printec that means Payten is less likely to buy a footprint ATM or POS tender at a loss-leading price this autumn, and more likely to hold list price to defend margin. Printec's bid teams in Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Romania should test aggressive but sustainable pricing on Q4 2026 tenders rather than assume they will be undercut.
signals.likelihood: Backlog is a leading indicator for Q3-Q4 2026 bidding behaviour
signals.followup: Re-read the backlog slides in the Q3 2026 deck (26/10/2026) to confirm whether the Q4 backlog also contracts.

signals.entity: SONET Slovakia, s.r.o. (Payten / ASEE Group subsidiary) — local-peer POS operator
signals.signal: NEW FINDING. Slovakia's Central Register of Contracts (crz.gov.sk) shows SONET Slovakia s.r.o. — listed in ASEE's H1 2026 report as a 100%-owned ASEE Group subsidiary — signing a steady run of 'Ramcova zmluva o dodavke a prevadzke POS terminalov' (framework contract for the supply and operation of POS terminals) with Slovak public buyers. Contracts published in the fresh window include: Verejna kniznica Mikulasa Kovaca 10/08/2026 (contract 19/2026); Mesto Zvolen 04/08/2026 (854/2026, plus implementing order 915/2026 for public toilets); Vychodoslovensky onkologicky ustav 06/07/2026 (108582/2026/S, EUR 203); Oravska poliklinika Namestovo 03/07/2026 (108666/2026/S); Rekreacne sluzby mesta Senica 01/07/2026 (58/2026); Bytovy podnik mesta Kosice 15/06/2026; Letisko Poprad-Tatry a.s. (Poprad-Tatry airport) 01/06/2026 (TAT/VR/50/2026). Earlier in 2026: Kancelaria Narodnej rady Slovenskej republiky (the Slovak Parliament's Chancellery) 15/04/2026, contract 26/2026, EUR 49,999.99 — the only one with a stated ceiling; the rest are published at EUR 0.00, i.e. pay-per-transaction frameworks with no fixed value. Separately, the same register shows Asseco Central Europe a.s. active with Slovak buyers in 2026 but exclusively in government/health/utility IT, not bank self-service: Financne riaditelstvo SR data-warehouse maintenance addendum no. 52, EUR 4,297,818.48, published 26/06/2026; Slovenska elektrizacna prenosova sustava registry-system service EUR 358,422.00 and works contract EUR 149,691.00, both 25/06/2026; Urad pre regulaciu hazardnych hier EUR 218,205.22 (10/07/2026) and EUR 20,774.52 (02/07/2026); Narodny bezpecnostny urad EUR 15,621.00 (10/07/2026).
signals.source_name: Centralny register zmluv (crz.gov.sk), supplier search 'sonet' and 'asseco', contracts published 01/01/2025-31/08/2026; individual contracts e.g. /zmluva/12665921/, /zmluva/12649737/, /zmluva/12412493/, /zmluva/12228902/
signals.implies: This answers the open question about Asseco in Slovakia two ways. First, Asseco Central Europe's 2026 Slovak wins are public-sector IT and are NOT a threat to Printec's self-service or payments lines — do not classify them as competitive losses. Second, the real Payten presence in Slovakia is SONET Slovakia, a local-peer POS operator that is quietly accumulating public-sector card-acceptance frameworks (municipalities, hospitals, an airport, a library, even Parliament) at zero headline value on a transaction-fee model. That is head-on against Printec's Verifone/Castles terminal estate and TMS proposition in Slovakia, and the zero-value framework format means these wins never show up in a tender-value sweep. Printec should build a Slovak public-sector card-acceptance play — terminals plus terminal management plus field service — and target the same buyer class before the frameworks renew.
signals.likelihood: Continuing: seven new frameworks in three months, with no sign of slowing
signals.followup: Pull the PDF text of the Zvolen (854/2026) and Parliament (26/2026) frameworks to learn SONET's per-transaction pricing and terminal brand; set a monthly CRZ alert on supplier 'SONET Slovakia'; check whether SONET also holds Czech public POS frameworks via smlouvy.gov.cz.

signals.entity: Monri Payments (Payten Holding S.A.) — merchant acceptance / fiscal ECR
signals.country: Croatia, Slovenia, Bosnia & Herzegovina, Serbia, Spain
signals.signal: ASEE's H1 2026 report discloses that on 23/04/2026 Payten Holding S.A. agreed to buy the remaining 25% of Monri Payments d.o.o. (Slovenia) from its non-controlling shareholder for EUR 750,000, paid 24/04/2026, taking Payten to 100%; the Slovenian entity Avera d.o.o. was renamed Monri Payments d.o.o. on 04/03/2026. Monri is the brand under which Payten runs its IPD service — a network of independent EFT POS terminals that, in ASEE's own words, 'enables merchants to replace two or more payment terminals at the point of sale with a single device connected directly to multiple acquirers'. The IPD+ECR lines are the only growing part of Payment Solutions (+EUR 2.7m in H1 2026). Monri's Croatian site is publishing actively through the delta window — a payment-gateway conversion webinar (18/08/2026), a 3DS explainer (11/08/2026), a Lider Fintech Talks appearance (24/07/2026) and inclusion in the Deloitte Technology Fast 500 EMEA (16/07/2026, no growth rate or revenue disclosed) — alongside a Croatian merchant push built on the Remaris electronic cash register and an eRacun (e-invoice) resale offer, riding Croatia's Fiskalizacija 2.0 mandate.
signals.source_name: ASEE H1 2026 Management Report (M&A note) + Monri Payments Croatia newsroom (WordPress feed, monri.hr)
signals.implies: Payten is deliberately shifting from selling bank-owned terminals to OPERATING a merchant-side terminal network it owns, monetised per transaction and bundled with fiscal cash registers and e-invoicing. A single Monri device replacing several acquirer terminals structurally shrinks the number of physical POS units Printec can sell into Croatia and Slovenia, and takes the terminal-management relationship away from the bank. Printec should respond by pitching managed acceptance and TMS-as-a-service to acquirers rather than terminal boxes, and should watch whether Monri's multi-acquirer model spreads to Bosnia and Serbia where Monri entities already exist.
signals.likelihood: Active and expanding through 2026 on the back of Croatia's Fiskalizacija 2.0 mandate
signals.followup: Establish how many live Monri IPD terminals exist in Croatia and Slovenia (not disclosed anywhere found); check whether Croatian or Slovenian acquirers are ceding terminal estates to Monri; assess whether Printec can offer a competing multi-acquirer single-terminal proposition with Verifone/Castles.

signals.entity: ASEE d.o.o. Serbia (Asseco SEE) — core payments software
signals.signal: ASEE announced on 16/06/2026 that it completed SEPA (Single Euro Payments Area) implementation for 14 banks in Serbia, with all 14 institutions going live on the same day to meet the regulatory deadline set for Serbia's SEPA entry. The delivery combined ASEE's Financial Gateway SaaS platform, extended to support SEPA, with enhancements inside the banks' core banking systems, enabling end-to-end SEPA Credit Transfer processing. No contract values or bank names are disclosed. This is consistent with the H1 2026 report, where Banking Solutions revenue grew fastest in SEE 'mainly due to operations in Serbia, Croatia and Macedonia', with roughly two-thirds of core-banking growth from implementation services.
signals.source_name: ASEE newsroom — 'ASEE Delivers SEPA Compliance for 14 Banks in Serbia'
signals.implies: Fourteen Serbian banks have just taken a same-day core-payments change from ASEE. That deepens ASEE's grip on the Serbian banking stack at exactly the moment Printec wants to sell x-core, OptiCash cash optimisation, INETCO transaction monitoring and Siron AML into that market — the incumbent will be first in the room for every adjacent payments project for the next two years. Printec's Serbian route to market is better framed as complementary infrastructure (ATM/recycler hardware, cash forecasting, device telemetry, AML) that ASEE does not supply, rather than head-to-head core-payments displacement.
signals.likelihood: Delivered; the account-control effect runs 12-24 months
signals.followup: Identify which 14 Serbian banks went live and whether any are Printec accounts (Raiffeisen Serbia x-core, AikBank NCR recyclers); pitch OptiCash and INETCO into the SEPA-driven payments-modernisation budgets these banks have just opened.

signals.entity: ASEE S.A. / Payten Holding — M&A and restructuring
signals.country: Bosnia & Herzegovina, Serbia, Slovenia, Albania, Portugal
signals.signal: The H1 2026 report (published 31/07/2026) discloses three structural moves. (1) On 22/04/2026 ASEE S.A. agreed to buy the remaining 40% of BS Telecom Solutions d.o.o. Sarajevo from non-controlling shareholders for EUR 8,497,000, with the share transfer completed 30/04/2026, taking ASEE to 100%. (2) On 24/04/2026 Payten Holding took Monri Payments d.o.o. (Slovenia) to 100% for EUR 750,000. (3) On 01/06/2026 Payten d.o.o. Novi Beograd and Afusion d.o.o. Beograd merged, continuing as Payten d.o.o. Novi Beograd (no consolidated-accounts impact). The Q2 deck additionally lists remaining non-controlling-interest put-option liabilities in EUR millions — Dwelt B&H 8.1, Ifthenpay Portugal 4.7, BS Telecom Solutions B&H 2.9, Helius Systems Albania 2.9 — i.e. a further pipeline of minority buyouts. ASEE's subsidiary list confirms Payten holds operating entities in Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Slovenia, Romania, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Turkey, Spain, Portugal and Latin America, with ASEE (non-Payten) entities in Albania, Bulgaria, Kosovo and a small Ukrainian subsidiary (Askepnet), described as not material.
signals.source_name: ASEE H1 2026 Management Report, 'Significant Events' and Group structure sections; Q2 2026 investor presentation (NCI put options)
signals.implies: Payten/ASEE is buying out its local minority partners and consolidating legal entities across Printec's footprint — a group tightening control ahead of a push rather than retrenching, even while its hardware lines shrink. The Bosnian consolidation (BS Telecom, Dwelt) matters most: Bosnia is where ASEE's revenue actually fell in H1, so expect a harder commercial push there in 2027. Printec should treat Bosnia and Montenegro as contested-but-winnable for NCR recyclers, x-core and managed services now, before the consolidated Bosnian unit re-arms.
signals.likelihood: Buyouts done; the remaining put options (Dwelt, Helius Albania) point to further consolidation within 12-24 months
signals.followup: Profile Dwelt d.o.o. Banja Luka and Helius Systems Sh.p.k. Tirana — neither appears in the 164-name competitor roster — and determine whether either sells anything Printec bids (POS, self-service, field services) in BiH/Albania.

signals.entity: Payten d.o.o. Beograd-Novi Beograd (PIB 110428879) — inside the National Bank of Serbia
signals.signal: Payten d.o.o. Beograd-Novi Beograd (PIB 110428879, registered 03/01/2018, activity code 6203 'management of computer equipment', owner Payten Holding Spolka Akcyjna) holds a contract with the National Bank of Serbia taken below the public-procurement threshold / under an exemption, so neither the subject nor the value is published — Serbian below-threshold and exempt contracts are not subject to publication. What IS published is the NBS 2026 procurement plan, which for 2026 carries several card- and payments-infrastructure workstreams in Q1 open procedure: an upgrade of the Cortex system's STIP software module ('stand-in processing', the fallback that authorises card transactions when the issuer's own host is unreachable) to support DinaCard-CUP chip payment cards; 'POS Terminali'; consumables for matrix, POS and RFID printers; and extension of the payment-systems software plus a system supporting the connection of NBS payment infrastructure to the EU's TARGET Instant Payment Settlement platform for SEPA entry. NOTE: the plan documents do not name a supplier, so the link between the Payten contract and any specific line above is NOT established — treat the Payten-Cortex association as unverified.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Serbia — Plan nabavki 2026, version 9 (PDF, nbs.rs); company registry entry for Payten d.o.o. (Companywall Serbia)
signals.implies: A named direct competitor is embedded inside Serbia's central bank on card and payments infrastructure, in the same year the NBS is rewiring for SEPA and TARGET instant settlement. That is a reference position Payten will use against Printec at every Serbian commercial bank — and it sits next to workstreams Printec could serve (POS terminals, HSM/PCI via Thales, transaction monitoring via INETCO). Printec should register as an NBS supplier and bid the published open procedures rather than concede the central bank by default.
signals.likelihood: Contract exists now; the NBS 2026 open procedures were scheduled for Q1 2026 and their awards are the next observable trigger
signals.followup: Obtain the NBS contract register or an operator-assisted search of jnportal.ujn.gov.rs for supplier PIB 110428879 to establish the subject and value of the Payten contract; confirm independently whether 'Cortex' is an ASEE/Payten product or a third party's.

signals.signal: [STANDING — dated 2026] The Payten corporate newsroom has published nothing since 16/06/2026, so there is no new named footprint win from Payten itself in the 24/07-31/08/2026 delta window. Its five most recent items are: Paratika's 'Unlimited Payment Link' for Turkey (16/06/2026), Payten and Paratika winning gold and bronze at the 2025 WSpark Awards, the 'Your Revenue Engineer' payment-orchestration framework built on Payten's Smart Switch multi-acquirer architecture (16/06/2026), Payten SoftPOS at Halkbank AD Skopje branded 'Halk Mobi POS' (17/03/2026), and Chip Card's ISO 9001 and PCI PIN re-certifications in Serbia (17/03/2026). The Halkbank Skopje SoftPOS date, flagged as unanchored in the previous run, is now confirmed at 17/03/2026 on the dated primary article; the piece states 'first results are encouraging' but discloses no merchant or transaction counts.
signals.source_name: Payten newsroom — 'Payten SoftPOS at Halkbank Skopje, Macedonia' and adjacent news items
signals.implies: Payten's SoftPOS (software that turns an ordinary Android phone into a contactless card-acceptance terminal, removing the need for hardware) is live at Halkbank in North Macedonia and its Smart Switch orchestration lets a merchant route through several acquirers at once — both erode the case for buying physical Verifone/Castles terminals. But the newsroom silence since mid-June means Payten is not currently publicising new footprint bank wins, which is consistent with the ATM/POS revenue retreat in the H1 report. Printec's counter in North Macedonia and Serbia is terminal management, certification and field service — the operational layer SoftPOS does not remove.
signals.likelihood: Live; no new announcements expected before the Q3 results
signals.followup: Ask Halkbank AD Skopje and other MK acquirers whether SoftPOS is displacing hardware or adding new micro-merchants; monitor the Payten newsroom monthly (note it is not WordPress and has no API).

signals.signal: The full subsidiary schedule in ASEE's H1 2026 report shows the group has NO operating entity in Greece, Cyprus, Austria or Hungary, and only one Ukrainian subsidiary, Askepnet TOV, which the report explicitly describes as immaterial to the Group's financial statements (ASEE states it does not conduct business operations in Russia, Belarus or Ukraine). Payten-branded entities exist in Bosnia, Croatia, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Slovenia, Romania, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Turkey and Western Europe/LatAm; ASEE-branded entities cover Albania, Bulgaria and Kosovo.
signals.source_name: ASEE H1 2026 Management Report — Group structure and Ukraine risk disclosure
signals.implies: Five of Printec's seventeen footprint countries — Greece, Cyprus, Austria, Hungary and Ukraine — carry no Payten delivery entity at all, so in those markets Printec's real rivals are Mellon, Euronet, Diebold Nixdorf, Worldline/Cardlink and the local players, not Payten. Bid teams in Athens, Nicosia, Vienna, Budapest and Kyiv should stop pricing against a Payten shadow.
